findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing custom grant providers
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is an extension SPI, and this adds a new abstract `getShortcut()` method. Existing third-party grant factories compiled against the previous interface will fail with `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` invokes the method; providers rebuilt without implementing it will not compile. Provide a backward-compatible default method and handle its absence/unknown result, or otherwise establish an explicit migration path before making token issuance depend on this method.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to the fixed two-character wire format
findings.body: The encoder concatenates `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` directly into the token ID, while the decoder unconditionally requires a six-character context and extracts exactly two characters for the grant shortcut. No validation enforces this requirement, and the factory interface documentation even says shortcuts are usually three letters. A custom grant provider returning (for example) `foo` will successfully issue IDs such as `onrtfoo:<uuid>`, but those IDs can never be decoded by this provider because their context length is seven. Enforce exactly two-character unique shortcuts during factory initialization/registration, or encode the context in a format that supports variable-length shortcuts.

findings.title: Removing the public Context copy constructor breaks grant implementations
findings.body: The public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context)` constructor was removed. Custom OAuth2 grant implementations using that constructor will no longer compile after an upgrade, and already-built implementations will fail at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError` when they attempt to create the copy. Retain the constructor, including the new `grantType` field in the copy, unless this is intentionally released as a documented incompatible SPI change.

findings.title: Access-token event matcher does not verify the grant shortcut
findings.body: The six-character context puts the grant shortcut at indexes 4-5, but this matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which includes the final token-type character and only the first grant character. It also returns `false` when that incorrectly extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Consequently the updated event assertions accept IDs with an incorrect grant shortcut (for example, an authorization-code expectation accepts `onrtzz:<uuid>`) and do not test the feature they were added to cover. Compare `substring(4, 6)` to the expected shortcut and return that comparison result.
